beginner.headline: Tomorrow (Sat Oct 17): conditional for beginners. Best 7:00–10:30 AM around the 9:24 AM high (1.8 ft), with the long-period south swell easing from tonight's peak. Breezy NE trades (~20 mph, model gusts to the upper 20s) all day mean seaward drift. Late morning conditional; from 12:30 PM not recommended. Evening forecast, lower confidence; the morning on-site check decides.
beginner.recommendation: Plan on the morning: 7:00–10:30 AM has the most water over the reef (9:24 AM high, 1.8 ft) and the south swell will be past its Friday-evening peak. Wind is the main limiter: NWS has NE around 20 mph Saturday and the Canoes model has gusts 26–28 mph from 6 AM; at Waikīkī that is cross-offshore, so expect steady seaward drift from the start rather than a calm early window. Buoys tonight still show 15 s south energy (51212 3.9 ft at 15 s, 51211 3.6 ft at 15 s at about 6:40 PM): even as it eases, expect lulls and occasional sets that reach the inside with more push than their size suggests. Watch several full set cycles (10+ minutes). DOH brown-water and bacteria advisories were reported Friday for the North Shore after heavy rain; nothing verified for Waikīkī, and the bacteria/sewage lists were not read, so check water color at Canoes and toward the Kūhiō drains and Ala Wai side. One student or a small group of strong adults; several students or children only if drift is low. Your on-site read overrides this report.

water.headline: No DOH brown-water advisory for Waikīkī on the list as read; North Shore advisories reported Friday; bacteria and sewage lists not read, so water quality at Canoes is not verified
water.statement: The DOH brown-water advisory list was read this evening: no Waikīkī entry and no open Oʻahu entry (only ʻAnini Beach, Kauaʻi). The Star-Advertiser reported on Oct 16 that DOH issued brown-water and bacteria advisories for Oʻahu's North Shore after heavy rain; that is not on the list as read and the beaches are not confirmed. A Waimea Bay bacteria advisory (North Shore) is reported by a third-party repost. None of these is a Waikīkī notice. The bacteria and sewage-spill lists were not read. Not finding an advisory does not prove the water is clean. Check water color.
water.why: The eha-cloud brown-water event list loaded (most recent rows read); the full advisory viewer covering bacteria and sewage did not load. Showers tonight are forecast mostly windward and mauka, which lowers but doesn't remove runoff risk at Waikīkī.
water.runoff: Brown, gray, cloudy or turbid water, or visible runoff: don't go in, advisory or not. DOH guidance: storm runoff can carry sewage and pathogens; stay out of affected water for 48–72 hours after rain stops.
